source_result: RV-377-041b (STAGE_DE_SMOOTH_V22_SYM5_S4.json, sha 094dd282b6c8cc57...) HELD 5/5 under the registered cost model; GMI-DA6 and gap G14: the registered cost model does not charge the FAILED DRAWS of a stochastic carrier, although gmi_microscope/vm.py::lifecycle_vector already carries B_search and B_failed_candidates
original_hypothesis: RV-377-041b's verdict ('the stochastic particle row S3 is the cheapest admissible form wherever it is admissible, taking 14/56 to 56/56 frontier cells') is an artefact of charging ONE development run for a carrier that requires about 1/q of them. Charging the failed draws as B_search moves a one-time term of (1/q - 1) x D_draw into the intercept of S3's cost line; at the measured reliability this term is one to three orders of magnitude larger than the whole registered (H, r) cost of any competing row, so every cost clause of RV-377-041b fails and only its two non-cost clauses survive. The stochastic carrier is not the cheapest admissible form at scope; it is the most expensive one, and the registered frontier tables hid the cost in an uncharged lottery.
minimal_proposed_change: DECLARED module gmi_microscope/failed_draws.py. Corrected cost model (frozen here, applied to the D'/E' frontier of E_sym5 at machine seed 4, rows ROWS_V6, six registered columns): C'(row, col, H, r) = C(row, col, H, r) + B_search(row, col), with C the registered line desc + H*exec_q + r*upd_e + r*ver_e + (r/4)*rev_e (smooth.cost, unchanged) and B_search(row, col) = B_failed_candidates(row) * D_draw(row, col); B_failed_candidates(row) = (1/q_row - 1), the expected number of FAILED draws before the first admissible one under a geometric law with success probability q_row; D_draw(row, col) = R['exec'] + R['upd'] + R['ver'] + R['rev'], the total charged work of ONE complete run of the registered 16-event development protocol at that (row, col, largest ladder size). Deterministic rows have q = 1 exactly, hence B_search = 0 and B_failed_candidates = 0 and their cost lines are unchanged. The two terms are read from vm.lifecycle_vector called on the live Machine of each re-executed cell, so the charge is the ledger's own rather than a re-derivation. Two declared reliability indices are reported: q_cell = 1/32 (E_sym5 at size 8, the census cell that produced seed 4) and q_pooled = 10/192 (the whole 192-run census). Frontier rule: R-top (each row at its largest ladder size), protocol rule 17, unchanged from RV-377-041b so that the re-adjudication is like for like. Clause units: frontier CELLS (56 per column = 8 reuse horizons H in {1,2,4,8,16,32,64,128} x 7 revision rates r in {0,1,2,4,8,16,32}; 336 over six columns), DRAWS (counts of complete development runs), charged OPS (D_draw and B_search), reuse horizon H in queries per lifecycle, reliability q as a fraction of seeds. Receipt microscopes/results/STAGE_G14_FAILED_DRAW_CHARGING_V1.json.

why_justified: G14 is the only registered gap that can invert a published verdict rather than qualify it. RV-377-041b is cited in GMI_DOMAIN_ALGEBRA_EXECUTED_V1.md (GMI-DA6) and in the theory core's L8v2 as the executed evidence that a stochastic population carrier is the cheapest admissible form at low reliability; if the uncharged term reverses it, every downstream statement about 'the cost of intelligence at low reliability is paid in failed draws' is wrong in sign, not only in magnitude.

observed_outcome: Receipt STAGE_G14_FAILED_DRAW_CHARGING_V1.json (sha 54823356e063884d...). 6 of 8 clauses HOLD. (1) HOLDS: all 30 R-top cells re-executed from scratch reproduce STAGE_DE_SMOOTH_V22_SYM5_S4.json on every ledger coordinate and on capability. (2) FAILS: the asserted pooled rate 10/192 = 0.052083 with 1/q = 19.2 draws is WRONG. The census receipt's own per-cell counts are 1 + 2 + 0 + 4 + 1 + 1 = 9, and a recount over its 192 raw capability values against theta = 0.85 also gives 9, so q_pooled = 9/192 = 0.046875 and the expected number of development runs is 1/q = 21.3333, not 19.2. The clause's two interval assertions do hold: the exact Clopper-Pearson 95 percent interval on q_pooled is (0.021655, 0.087116), contained in (0.02, 0.10), i.e. 1/q within (11.48, 46.18) and so within (10, 50); and for the census cell that produced seed 4 (E_sym5 size 8, q = 1/32) the interval on q is (0.000791, 0.162171), whose upper end on 1/q is 1264.4 draws and does exceed 500. The clause fails on the quoted rate alone, and the quoted rate came from the committed record: RV-377-040's observed_outcome, GMI_DOMAIN_ALGEBRA_EXECUTED_V1 section 7 and the gap ledger's G2b all say '10 of 192 (about 5 percent)'. That is a real off-by-one in the programme's own published reliability index, now recorded in the receipt's defects_found_in_committed_records. (3) HOLDS: at q_cell = 1/32 the stochastic row S3 occupies 0 of 56 cells in each of the six columns, 0 of 336. (4) HOLDS: at q_pooled = 9/192 (the corrected rate, a LARGER charge than the frozen 10/192) also 0 of 336. (5) FAILS, and it could not have held however the cost came out: 'the committed frontier with S3 struck out' names the wrong object. Deleting S3 from a committed WINNER LIST empties every cell where S3 was the sole occupant, which is 246 of 336. The quantity the clause was reaching for -- the frontier RECOMPUTED over the admissible set with S3 removed -- agrees with the corrected frontier in 336 of 336 cells (0 differing), and is reported as no_collateral_movement_recomputed rather than used to rescue the clause. (6) HOLDS: the minimum break-even reliability q* = D_draw/(D_draw + Delta) over the registered grid is 0.8426 (B0), 0.8426 (B1), 0.6727 (B2), 0.5121 (B3), 0.4992 (P3), 0.4992 (U), all above 0.49; the carrier would have to be admissible on half its seeds to hold one cell and is admissible on one seed in thirty-two. (7) HOLDS: the r = 0 re-entry crossover is finite and above 10^6 in every column -- H** = 1.105e8 (B0, B1), 1.223e9 (B2), 4.472e7 (B3), 4.158e7 (P3, U). (8) HOLDS: RV-377-041b re-adjudicated clause by clause under the corrected cost -- clause 1 (S3 admissible at size 8, 0.9375, inadmissible at size 4, 0.3021) HOLDS; clause 2 (every non-S3 cell identical to V8_SYM5_H) HOLDS; clause 3 (14 of 56 B0 cells) FAILS at 0 of 56; clause 4 (B1 = B0, B3 a superset of B0 with count >= 14) FAILS at 0 B3 cells, although the B1 = B0 half remains true with both now empty of S3; clause 5 (r = 0 is S3 in all six columns, 48 of 48) FAILS at 0 of 48. Exactly 2 of 5 survive and they are exactly the two that are not cost claims. Charged magnitudes: D_draw = 39324 (B0/B1), 434996 (B2), 15912 (B3), 14795 (U/P3) ops per development run; at 31 failed draws B_search = 1219044 / 13484876 / 493272 / 458645, against a largest registered-grid lifecycle cost of about 5.1e4. DG-2 self-check on this receipt: on an extended grid reaching H = 4294967296 the stochastic row does win again -- 68 cells (B0, B1), 90 (B2), 93 (B3, P3, U) of 720 -- so the verdict '0 of 336' is a statement about H <= 128 and is reported with its crossover, not as a grid-free no-cell claim.
failure_class: two prediction-writing errors, both mine, both of classes the lane has already registered: clause 2 quoted a committed number instead of recomputing it from the census receipt (and the committed number is wrong), and clause 5 named the wrong object (a winner list rather than a recomputed frontier), which protocol rules 12 and 14 exist to catch
strongest_mundane_explanation: the correction is not subtle and needed no new measurement: one development run of the particle row costs 1.5e4 to 4.3e5 charged ops, and the carrier needs about 21 of them (32 at the cell rate) to produce one admissible machine, while the entire registered (H, r) lifecycle of the rows it was said to beat costs at most about 5.1e4. A one-time term two to four orders of magnitude above the whole competition can only produce a clean sweep in the other direction; the surprise is that the registered cost model let the claim stand at all
strongest_parent_explanation: Levin/OOPS search accounting and the biosphere burden vector: the cost of a realization obtained by sampling is the expected cost of the whole sampling procedure, not of the accepted sample. GMI-DA6's reliability index q is exactly the acceptance rate of that procedure, so 1/q is its expected trial count and (1/q - 1) x D_draw its discarded work. Charging it is the standard accounting, and the registered model's omission of it was the anomaly
measurement_validity_status: valid: the 30 committed cells were re-executed from scratch and reproduce exactly, B_search and B_failed_candidates are read from vm.lifecycle_vector on the live Machine ledger, all frontier arithmetic is exact rational, and the confidence intervals are exact-binomial (Clopper-Pearson bisected on Fractions to 1e-12)
mechanism_attribution: acceptance rate of the stochastic development procedure (q) x the charged work of one development run (D_draw) -> a one-time intercept B_search that exceeds every competing row's entire lifecycle cost by two to four orders of magnitude at every cell of the registered grid
new_invariant_learned: at scope the stochastic population carrier is never the cheapest admissible form once its failed draws are charged: it wins 0 of 336 registered cells at q = 1/32 and at q = 9/192, and its break-even reliability is q* in [0.4992, 0.8426] by column while its measured reliability is 1/32. The published pooled reliability of the carrier is 9 of 192 = 4.6875 percent (1/q = 21.33 draws), not the 10 of 192 = 5.2 percent (19.2 draws) carried by RV-377-040, GMI-DA6 and the gap ledger
new_theory_constraint: GMI-DA6 gains a second half: a stochastic carrier's frontier is a step function of q AND its cost line carries a q-dependent intercept B_search = (1/q - 1) x D_draw, so lowering the declared reliability moves the carrier into the admissible set and out of the cheap set at the same time. Protocol rule 20: a frontier table containing a stochastic row is invalid unless it charges B_search at the same declared q that admitted the row; a table that declares q for admissibility and charges q = 1 for cost is internally inconsistent. Theory core L4 gains the term; the sentence in RV-377-041b's new_theory_constraint that 'the cost of intelligence at low reliability is paid in failed draws' is correct and now executed -- with the sign the original record did not draw, namely that paying it removes the carrier from the frontier entirely
